---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Water Quality"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Water quality, or water purification, is valued as the nutrient retention ecosystems provide,
priced at what it would cost to treat the same load. Two nutrients are carried, nitrogen and
phosphorus, for the base year 2019, in 2019 US dollars. The calculation follows the authors'
current write-up and ports their Stata script, `analysis.do`, step by step.

## Quantity

Retained nutrient in kilograms, allocated to domestic use:

$$
\text{EstimatedRetention (kg)} = \text{TotalRetention (kg)} \times \text{DomesticWaterUseFraction}
$$

The domestic-water-use fraction is the AQUASTAT domestic share of withdrawals. It is an
allocation proxy: it does not show that the retained load would otherwise reach domestic
supply. The total
retention figures come from an InVEST NDR estimation upstream. A negative retention estimate is
treated as missing and a true zero is kept, so a country with a negative estimate for either
nutrient carries no value.

## Price

The authors collected treatment and avoided-treatment costs per kg of nitrogen and phosphorus
from the literature: 32 observations once converted, 17 for nitrogen and 15 for phosphorus. Each
is brought to US dollars per kg at the 2019 price level. Reported units go to kg. A price
reported in US dollars goes to local currency at the observation year's World Bank exchange
rate, and a price reported in euro by a country outside the euro goes to local currency through
the euro's own dollar rate. The World Bank GDP deflator moves the local-currency price to the
2019 price level. The Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian observations are reported in euro for
2008, before those countries adopted it. Each goes to its old currency through the euro's dollar
rate in 2008, is deflated there, and returns to euro at the old-currency-per-euro rate of the
year before adoption. The 2019 exchange rate then gives US dollars.

The observations are pooled in one benefit-transfer regression:

$$
\ln(\text{price}) = b_0 + b_\text{gdppc} \ln(\text{GDP per capita}_{2019}) + b_p \cdot \text{phosphorus}
$$

Each country's price is the conditional median, $\exp$ of the fitted value at its 2019 GDP per
capita, with the phosphorus term for phosphorus. On the staged inputs the fit gives
$b_0 = -3.6374$, $b_\text{gdppc} = 0.5903$ and $b_p = 1.0099$, as in the authors' log. A country
with no 2019 GDP per capita has no price.

## Valuation

$$
\text{GEP} = \text{price}_N \times N + \text{price}_P \times P
$$

with $N$ and $P$ the estimated retention after the negative estimates are set to missing. The sum
is missing when either term is.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `water_quality` service, all in
`global_invest/water_quality/price_transfer/` (provenance in its README):

- `water_quality_retention_path`, the per-country retention estimates (total, domestic share,
  estimated).
- `water_quality_raw_prices_path`, the authors' raw cost observations.
- `water_quality_gdp_deflator_path`, `water_quality_exchange_rate_path` and
  `water_quality_gdp_per_capita_path`, the three World Bank series the script reads.
- `water_quality_reference_gep_path`, the authors' exported table, which the tests reproduce.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, the two prices per kg, the retention used, each
nutrient's value and `water_quality_gep`, their sum. The log records the regression's
coefficients and the number of observations.

## Checks

The port reproduces the authors' exported table on all 250 countries: identical missing values
(178 valued, 10 zero, 62 missing), prices within 2e-6 relative (the script stores them in single
precision) and the same total to 1e-7. `water_purification_gep` raises if an estimated retention
stops equalling its total times the domestic fraction.

## Taken as given

The retention totals. The authors' folder carries the InVEST NDR outputs but no script or run
log for them, so the InVEST version and the units of the retention rasters are not established
here.

## Limitations

- The regression rests on 32 observations, and 18 of them come from one report's four values
  (Gren 2008, the lower bounds of its sewage-treatment cost ranges). Its R² is 0.156, and the
  income and phosphorus coefficients have p-values of 0.106 and 0.095.
- Two of the three Chinese nitrogen observations price ammonia nitrogen, not total nitrogen:
  Ouyang 2020 (NH-N, from the NDRC treatment costs) and Li 2025 ("the cost of ammonia nitrogen
  purification is 7910 CNY/t"). The retention they are applied to is total nitrogen.
- The third, Li 2024 (Tonglu County, 2021), enters as a nitrogen price of 9,572.92 CNY/t. In
  that paper 9,572.92 CNY/t is the treatment cost of COD (chemical oxygen demand), and its
  ammonia-nitrogen cost is 8,000 CNY/t. Measured with this pipeline, 8,000 in its place gives a
  total 0.65% lower, and dropping the row gives one 6.8% higher. The observation stays as the
  authors entered it until they correct it.
- The value adds the nitrogen and phosphorus terms. That is valid only if the two unit costs are
  incremental and pollutant-specific. Gren 2008, the source of 18 of the 32 observations, lists
  increased cleaning at sewage treatment plants among the measures that affect both nutrients,
  costed as annualised investment, and the report does not state how a shared investment is
  split between its per-kg nitrogen and per-kg phosphorus costs. Whether the sum counts shared
  treatment spending twice is therefore not established.
- The prices are treatment and avoided-treatment costs. A reviewer's comment linked from the
  write-up suggests constructed wetlands as a lower-cost replacement, which would put the
  replacement cost below these prices.
- The domestic share allocates retention to domestic use as a proxy. It is not a measured
  delivery of the retained load to domestic supply.
- Which retention definition produced the 2019 table is not established: the committed code
  takes the base run's load minus export, while the write-up describes the difference in export
  between a scenario and the baseline.
- Earlier versions of this account priced retention at the committed table's per-country prices
  and kept negative estimates. That construction is superseded by the authors' current method.
